#!/usr/bin/env python3
import argparse
import construct

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--a', type=int, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--b', type=int, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--c', type=str, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    format1 = construct.Int8ul.build(args.a)
    format2 = construct.Int8ul.build(args.b)
    length = len(args.c)
    format3 = construct.Bytes(length).build(args.c.encode())
    print(format1)
    print(format2)
    print(format3)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

whether only the FIRST bad char is reported. Also determine what 'expected X, found Y' uses.

Use `[...str].length` / iterate with for..of / Array.from — never `.length` and never a UTF-16 index. stdout must be EMPTY on every failure. A naive port that writes line 1 and line 2 as soon as they are built, then fails on --c, will print `b'\x01'\nb'\x01'\n` to stdout and diverge. All three values must be fully computed (and all three errors checked, in order a→b→c) BEFORE anything is written to stdout.
The frame line number in the FormatFieldError template differs between --a (line 12) and --b (line 13). A single shared error-formatting helper that hardcodes one number will be wrong half the time.

`_build` appears TWICE in the FormatFieldError traceback with DIFFERENT line numbers: 1165 in the inner `struct.error` traceback and 1167 in the outer chained one. Easy to copy-paste the same number to both.

UnicodeEncodeError has two distinct grammatical forms and the plural one DROPS the character repr entirely: singular `can't encode character '\udcff' in position 1`, plural `can't encode characters in position 0-2`. The switch is on the length of the first maximal run of bad bytes, not on the total count of bad bytes.
Only the FIRST run of unencodable code points is reported. `a\xffb\xfec` must report position 1 and stop scanning — do not report the last one or a combined range.

StreamError frames include construct/core.py 452/464/970/195, but UnicodeEncodeError has NO construct frames at all (only test8.py 21 and 15) — because `.encode()` raises before `.build()` is called. Both are on source line 15, so keying the traceback shape off the line number alone is wrong.

A port that echoes process.argv text will diverge. Values can exceed Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (`-99999999999999999999999999` is printed in full) — use BigInt for the range check and the decimal rendering.

Node's `process.argv` lossily converts invalid UTF-8 bytes to U+FFFD, which is a VALID code point and would produce a StreamError (`expected 1, found 3`) instead of the correct UnicodeEncodeError. You must read raw bytes from /proc/self/cmdline (NUL-separated) and do your own surrogateescape decode. Note U+FFFD passed legitimately (`ef bf bd`) really does give StreamError expected 1 found 3 — so you cannot distinguish the two after Node's mangling.

The UTF-8 validity check must be STRICT: reject overlongs (`c0 80`, `e0 80 80`), surrogate encodings (`ed a0 80`..`ed bf bf`), and >U+10FFFF (`f4 90 80 80`, `f5 80 80 80`). But `ed 9f bf` (U+D7FF) and `f4 8f bf bf` (U+10FFFF) are VALID. A lenient decoder will route these to the wrong error template.

Every invalid byte becomes exactly ONE surrogate code point — the run length equals the count of consecutive bytes not consumed by a valid sequence. `c2 41` gives a run of 1 (singular form) because the `41` is valid ASCII, while `f0 9f 41` gives a run of 2. Getting the maximal-subpart consumption wrong flips singular/plural.

The `[PYI-{PID}:ERROR]` trailer is on stderr (not stdout), appears on all three templates, and its PID is non-deterministic — any byte-for-byte stderr comparison must mask it. stdout, by contrast, is fully deterministic (and empty for all these cases).
Surrogate hex in the repr is LOWERCASE and always 4 digits: `'\udc8a'`, `'\udcef'` — not `\uDC8A`. JS `.toString(16)` gives lowercase but you must zero-pad to 4.
